title: Slice panic text differs from native when gc constant-folds a sub-word out-of-range index (native message is the wrong one)
claim: With a compile-time-known uint8/uint16/int8 index (e.g. var i uint8 = 200; s[:i]) native gc panics with boundsError text reporting index 0 ('[:0] with length 3'); the generic wrapper reports the true index ('[:200] with length 3'). Same panic site and type; only the Error() text differs, and the wrapper is the correct one. Non-constant indices of every width produce identical messages.

title: Tainted strings.Join of one element returns a fresh clone where the stdlib returns the element itself
claim: JoinString only takes the alias fast path when separator == ""; for a single tainted element with a non-empty separator it clones. Content is equal; identity differs (unsafe-only) and costs one extra len(s) allocation per tainted call.

title: Inactive BytesToString heap-allocates where native string(b) stays on the stack (duplicate of hooks-yml-operators-F4 / prop-concat-conv-json-F1; fix probe clarifies scope)
claim: Native non-escaping string(b) = 0 allocs; BytesToString = 1 alloc with IAST inactive. Evaluating string(value) inside the !HasValues() branch restores 0 allocs, but the same restructuring of Concat2 regresses it from 0 to 1 alloc, so the fix belongs only in BytesToString.
